TODO

Source: TODO.md

  • Look into making the root path used for immediateCondition RDS files (immediateConditionsPath(), which defaults to file.path(tempdir(), ".future", "immediateConditions")) configurable, e.g. via an R option, rather than hardcoded to tempdir() everywhere it’s called from MulticoreFutureBackend (readImmediateConditions() / saveImmediateCondition()).

  • IDEA: Let an object/function carry its own forwarding hints via an attribute, e.g. attr(fcn, "future_meta") <- list(packages = "somepkg", globals = c("extra_obj"), options = c("digits", "somepkg.verbose")). Note (2026-10-12): this should probably be reconciled with, rather than compete with, the already-proposed resources mechanism - see https://www.futureverse.org/roadmap/resources.html and https://www.jottr.org/2026/08/11/roadmap-resources-memory/. resources<-() already sets attr(fcn, "resources") on a function (even third-party code, e.g. resources(cv.glmnet) <- function(x, ...) memory(4 * object.size(x))), consulted automatically by resources()/futurize() at dispatch time - the identical architecture this future_meta idea independently arrived at, so far scoped to compute resources (memory now; walltime, scratch space, GPU cores/memory later) rather than packages/globals/options. Rather than a second, parallel attribute, extending resources() itself to also cover “what this function/call needs forwarded” is probably the better path - same resources(fcn) <- function(...) ... pattern, same consultation point, just a different payload than memory/walltime/GPU. Filed as a generalized idea (declaring soft/ indirect dependencies instead of inferring them via static analysis) at future-ideas#1117, with this reconciliation noted as a follow-up comment there.

    • Package-level declarations (not just function-level): attach resources to the package’s .onLoad() function as the default, easiest-to-understand convention - no new API, just resources<-() applied to the one function every package can rely on as a stable, well-known, namespace-resident anchor (asNamespace(pkg)$.onLoad; a package without one can add a trivial .onLoad() purely to carry the attribute). This means inspecting it requires the package’s namespace to be loaded (harmlessly, since attributes don’t affect how a function is called) - fine in the common case where the package is already loaded for real reasons, a minor acceptable cost in the rarer fully-transitive case (inspecting a Suggests-of-a-Suggests that nothing has loaded yet). Ship this first, since it needs no new file format or build tooling. Two load-free optimizations can be layered on top later, for packages that specifically want to avoid the load: a Config/<tool>/<field> DESCRIPTION field (e.g. Config/future/options: progressr.enable, following the existing Config/testthat/edition-style convention) for simple name-only declarations; and, for declarations that need actual code (e.g. a memory-estimator closure), a sidecar file (inst/resources.rds, or an install-time-generated Meta/resources.rds alongside the Meta/*.rds files every installed package already has) storing deparsed source text, ideally auto-compiled from the same .onLoad()-attribute source at build/install time (the roxygen2-comments-to-.Rd-files pattern) rather than hand- maintained. See the follow-up comments on #1117 for the fuller writeup. Static-code inspection (globals::globalsOf() et al., driving getGlobalsAndPackages()) can miss globals/packages that are only referenced indirectly (e.g. via do.call(), NSE, or other non-lexical lookups) - future_meta would let the object/function author explicitly declare what must always be forwarded, regardless of what static analysis finds (or misses). The same attribute could also name R options that should travel with the object/function to the worker, which would double as one concrete, scoped answer to the general “pass options() down to futures” problem in #134/#480 (see below) - scoped to “this specific object/function needs these specific options”, rather than solving automatic/global options propagation for every future.

    • Relates to: #134 (“R options: options() are not passed down to futures - should they?”) and #480 (“future() arguments for passing R options and environment variables”), which are about forwarding options at the future()/plan() call site, not attached to a specific object.

    • Also somewhat adjacent to the declare(prologue(...))/ declare(epilogue(...)) idea in future-ideas#1035, which annotates expressions passed to futurize()/future() rather than objects/functions themselves.

    • Open questions: where would future_meta be read from - only top-level globals, or also objects found while walking into packages/environments during getGlobalsAndPackages()? Would options listed this way need “value to forward” vs. just “name to forward” (cf. future(..., options = c("foo", BAR = 42L)) in #480)? How would conflicting future_meta from multiple objects in the same future be reconciled? Does this need to be an attribute specifically (surviving serialization, but easy to lose via copying/subsetting), or would a registry/S3-method-based declaration (e.g. future_meta.my_class <- function(x) ...) be more robust?

    • Concrete worked example, and the one that actually makes this useful rather than redundant: attach the metadata to progressr’s progressor() generator function itself (the function exported as progressr::progressor), not to the closure it returns. Whether progress reporting does anything depends on the progressr.enable option, which is not propagated to multisession/cluster workers today (that’s exactly the #134 gap) - so a fresh progressor() call made inside worker-executed code (e.g. deep in a package’s call stack, or code injected by progressify()) resolves enable against the worker’s own, independent option default and doesn’t know the master already disabled progress, paying full overhead for updates nobody will see.

      The fix only works if the metadata sits on the generator, because only the generator is referenced by the future expression before the call happens - by the time a returned progressor object p exists, its no-op-ness is already permanently baked in, so attaching metadata there is too late to change anything. Attaching it to the generator also sidesteps the serialization question entirely: progressr::progressor is an exported, unchanged function living inside the progressr package namespace, so a future_meta attribute set on it once (as part of the installed package) is automatically present, identically, on every worker that loads progressr too - nothing about the attribute itself needs to be shipped across the wire. What does need forwarding is the current value of progressr.enable, read from the master session, and the trigger for forwarding it is exactly future’s existing globals/packages analysis noticing that the future expression references progressor (already needed today, to know the worker must have the progressr package attached). At that point future would snapshot getOption("progressr.enable") on the master and arrange for it to be set on the worker (e.g. via an auto-generated options(progressr.enable = <value>) prologue) before the expression runs - so that when progressor() executes fresh inside the worker, it resolves enable to the master’s actual value and correctly returns void_progressor there too.

    • Limitation: nested futures. The detection-and-forward trigger only sees whatever a single static analysis pass can find at the moment a given future() call is made. If an inner future’s body is written directly inside an outer future’s literal source (even several future() calls deep), the outer-level static walk of the full parse tree still finds a nested progressor reference fine - static analysis doesn’t stop at sub-call boundaries. But if the inner future is only created dynamically, at runtime, deep inside the outer future’s own execution (a data-dependent branch, a generic recursive dispatcher, an expression only constructed via do.call()/NSE on the fly), there is nothing for any ancestor’s static analysis to find in advance, because the code that would contain the progressor() reference doesn’t exist yet when the check runs. Worse, even if detection is implemented generically (so every future() call, including ones made from inside a worker, re-runs its own check against its own current option value), the chain only propagates correctly if every ancestor level’s detection already fired: if the outermost (master) expression has no textual trace that triggers forwarding, worker-1 never receives the forwarded value, so even though worker-1’s own subsequent nested future() call will correctly detect progressor in whatever it dispatches next (that expression is concrete by the time it’s created, so detection there is trivial), it has only its own unforwarded, default progressr.enable to propagate onward - the chain breaks at the first invisible link, not just at the end.

    • Refinement: move the trigger from “is this function referenced in this expression” to “is this package currently loaded in my session” - a session-level fact, knowable the instant any future() call fires, at any nesting level, without needing to see what code will run. In practice a package is usually loaded once, early (e.g. library(progressr) in the master, or requireNamespace("progressr")/progressr::progressor() deep in worker code), so this is far more likely to already be true at every relevant nesting level than “does this specific sub-expression textually mention progressor.” This does not come for free from today’s existing package-to-worker forwarding, though: per R/protected_api-globals.R (around where packagesOf(globals) is computed and then filtered by attachedPackages()/search()), which packages get attached to a worker is already derived from the same static per-expression globals detection, intersected with currently-attached packages used only as a filter - it is not a blanket “whatever’s loaded in my session also gets attached on the worker” rule. For this idea to actually deliver the improvement, the new options-forwarding check would need to be independent of that pipeline: at every future() call, separately ask “which packages are currently loaded, and does any of them declare a package-level future_meta object naming options to forward?” rather than reusing/being limited by packagesOf(globals). Also, that check should be against loadedNamespaces(), not search() (which is what the existing attachedPackages() helper checks): idiomatic package-internal code calling another package’s export typically does so via pkg::fcn() (e.g. progressr::progressor(), which is what progressify()-generated code would plausibly do) without ever attaching that package to the search path, so a search()-based check would miss it entirely. Even with this refinement, the very first hop (master to its immediate worker) still needs something to establish that the package is relevant there at all; in the fully pathological case where the master’s own code has zero textual or loaded-namespace trace of progressr (unlikely in practice, since the master almost always already calls with_progress()/handlers() itself), even a loadedNamespaces()-based check has nothing to trigger on at that outermost hop - but that is a much narrower edge case than the per-function version had, and every hop after the first is fixed.
